scope: C9 arbitrary-independent-amplitude all-N odd-cubic Pfaffian family; not mere existence of solitons for the cubic equation
wording: Previously unproved in this project; not established to have been previously open in the literature.

sources.source: Hietarinta 1997 primary account, arXiv:solv-int/9708006, section 4.2, equation 37
sources.relation: Same cubic coupled pair at a_H=0, (x_H,y_H,t_H)=(x-c1*t,c3*t,y); two seed types and three-soliton search. No inspected all-N arbitrary-amplitude Pfaffian formula.

AIP abstract considers an odd first polynomial and a quadratic second polynomial. This alone does not verify the precise attribution of the quartic factorized pair appearing in the 1997 summary to paper II rather than its other cited 1987/1990 sources.

sources.source: Peng, Zhang, Gegenhasi and Liu 2008, doi:10.1016/j.physleta.2008.01.090
sources.relation: Abstract claims Wronskian N-solitons and a proposed Lax representation for a Hietarinta mKdV-type equation. The exact seed parameters and equality/containment relative to C9 are not established.
sources.author_record_observation: Entry65 lists title/pages, but inspected HTML has no paper/PDF/download link. It lists Peng as a former master's student; no corresponding author-hosted manuscript was found.

sources.source: Gegenhasi, Hu and Wang 2007, A (2+1)-dimensional sinh-Gordon equation and its Pfaffian generalization, doi:10.1016/j.physleta.2006.07.031
sources.access: metadata; original full text inaccessible; equation attribution read in Wang-Yu-Zhu2023
sources.relation: Wang-Yu-Zhu2023 Eq5 attributes (Dy+Dx^2)F.G=0 and [Dt(Dy+Dx^2)+2Dx]F.G=0 to this source. That is a quadratic first operator with nonzero remainder, not the zero-remainder cubic pair of C9. Original Pfaffian generalization's complete scope remains uninspected.

sources.source: Wang, Yu and Zhu 2023, General Soliton and (Semi-)Rational Solutions of a (2+1)-Dimensional Sinh-Gordon Equation, doi:10.1007/s44198-023-00147-z
sources.relation: All-N Gram determinant theorem for the preceding quadratic/nonzero-remainder pair. This inspected theorem is not a theorem for C9's cubic/common-factor pair; no parameter dictionary or limiting reduction to the C9 family was established.

sources.source: Gegenhasi and Tam 2006, A pfaffian solution to the modified discrete BKP equation, doi:10.1016/j.chaos.2005.08.084
sources.relation: Pfaffian solutions of a modified discrete BKP equation. Institutional record supplies DOI but no manuscript. A continuum or coefficient dictionary to C9 was not verified; cannot dismiss as unrelated nor count as settling.
